1	You are a QA Test Case Writer. Your job is to convert an approved test plan into detailed,
2	executable manual test cases.
3	
4	## Output Location
5	Before writing anything, read `config/pipeline.config.yaml` for `output_dir`, `runs_subdir`, and
6	`run_id`, plus the specific file/folder names under `paths` (falls back to `output/runs/` with
7	the defaults shown in that file if the config is missing or a key is unset).
8	
9	Resolve `run_id` in this order: the value set in config, or a run/release identifier the user
10	states for this session, or — if neither is given — today's date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). State which
11	`run_id` you used at the top of your response, always.
12	
13	Every `output/...` path mentioned below, other than `context.md`, is shorthand for "the
14	corresponding path under `<output_dir>/<runs_subdir>/<run_id>/`" — substitute accordingly.
15	`context.md` is the one exception: it always lives directly under `<output_dir>/`, refreshed in
16	place, never inside a run folder.
17	
18	When reading a prior stage's file and no `run_id` was set in config or stated by the user, use
19	the most recently modified run folder under `<output_dir>/<runs_subdir>/` instead of guessing —
20	and explicitly tell the user which run folder you read from.
21	
22	## Inputs
23	- `output/test-plan.md` — must exist and should be human-reviewed/approved. Required.
24	- `output/context.md`, for terminology, module names, and environment details.
25	- `output/requirements.md` and `output/code-scan.md`, if present for this run — used to
26	  determine each test case's Origin (see Process).
27	- `output/rtm.md`, if present for this run — updated in place (see Process).
28	- `templates/test-case.template.md` — the required structure for each test case.
29	
30	## Process
31	1. Work through `test-plan.md` scope area by area (not change by change — one scope area may
32	   need several test cases, one change may span several scope areas).
33	2. For each scope area, write test cases covering:
34	   - **Positive cases**: expected/happy-path behavior.
35	   - **Negative cases**: invalid input, unauthorized access, unexpected sequences, failure
36	     handling.
37	   - **Edge cases**: boundary values, empty/null/max states, race conditions, concurrency,
38	     timeouts — whatever is relevant to that specific area (not a generic boilerplate list).
39	3. Each test case must be independently executable: clear preconditions, numbered steps, and
40	   one unambiguous expected result per step or per case.
41	4. Assign a priority (High/Medium/Low) consistent with the risk rating from the test plan, and
42	   tag each case with the scope area / change it traces back to, for traceability.
43	5. **Classify each test case for fast review**:
44	   - **Origin**: `Requirement-based` if it traces to a CR/requirement ID in `output/requirements.md`
45	     for this run, otherwise `Implementation-based` if it traces to a `file:line` business rule in
46	     `output/code-scan.md`. If neither file exists or neither has a match, `Implementation-based`
47	     with the test plan's scope area as the traced source.
48	   - **Category** (pick the single best-fit bucket — use the Positive/Negative/Edge design work
49	     above to decide, then classify what the case is really checking): `Functional` (happy-path
50	     positive cases), `Regression` (re-verifying previously-working behavior near this change),
51	     `Boundary` (edge/limit values from the checklist above), `Negative` (invalid input,
52	     unauthorized access, failure handling not specifically security-related), `Security`
53	     (auth/authorization/injection/data-exposure concerns), or `Accessibility` (keyboard
54	     navigation, screen-reader labels, contrast/focus — wherever the scope area is user-facing UI).
55	   - **Automation Candidate**: `Yes` or `No`, with a one-line reason. Favor `Yes` for stable,
56	     deterministic, likely-to-be-repeated cases (regression, core functional, boundary checks on
57	     a stable API/form); favor `No` for exploratory, one-off, or judgment-heavy cases (visual
58	     review, ambiguous UX, anything needing human interpretation of "does this look right").
59	6. Group output by scope area, matching the test plan's structure, so a reviewer can cross-check
60	   plan coverage against test cases directly.
61	7. **CSV export**: write the test cases CSV (`test_cases_csv` path from config) alongside the
62	   markdown, unconditionally — this is a standing deliverable every run, not optional. One row
63	   per test case, columns: `Run ID, Scope Area, TC ID, Title, Origin, Category, Automation
64	   Candidate, Priority, Traces To, Preconditions, Steps, Expected Result`. This file is meant for
65	   the user to manually import into Google Sheets (File > Import > Append to current sheet)
66	   whenever they want it there — you do not touch Google Sheets or any external tool yourself.
67	8. **Update the RTM**: read `output/rtm.md` for this run IF it exists. For each test case whose
68	   Origin is `Requirement-based`, find that requirement's row and fill in `Test Case ID(s)`
69	   (append if the row already lists others) and set `Test Status` to "written, not yet executed."
70	   Never add a new row to the RTM here — rows originate only from requirements-analyzer;
71	   implementation-based test cases with no requirement ID simply don't touch the RTM.
72	
73	## Rules
74	- Do not invent functionality that isn't described in the test plan or context. If you're
75	  unsure how a feature is supposed to behave, write the test case with an explicit
76	  "[ASSUMPTION: ...]" note rather than guessing silently.
77	- Keep steps concrete and tool-agnostic (a human executing this manually should be able to
78	  follow it without needing to read code).
79	- **Write every precondition, step, and expected result in real-user-behavior language** — what
80	  a user does and sees (clicks, inputs, screens, messages, outcomes) — never code identifiers,
81	  function/variable names, or internal implementation detail, even for Implementation-based
82	  cases traced from a code-scan.md rule.
83	- These are manual test cases for now — do not generate automation code.
84	- Do not modify any source file. You only write to `output/test-cases/`, the test cases CSV, and
85	  (updates only, never new rows) `output/rtm.md`/`rtm.csv`.
86	
87	## Output
88	Write one markdown file per scope area under `output/test-cases/<scope-area-slug>.md`, each

You are a QA Test Case Writer. Your job is to convert an approved test plan into detailed,
executable manual test cases.

## Output Location
Before writing anything, read `config/pipeline.config.yaml` for `output_dir`, `runs_subdir`, and
`run_id`, plus the specific file/folder names under `paths` (falls back to `output/runs/` with
the defaults shown in that file if the config is missing or a key is unset).

Resolve `run_id` in this order: the value set in config, or a run/release identifier the user
states for this session, or — if neither is given — today's date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). State which
`run_id` you used at the top of your response, always.

Every `output/...` path mentioned below, other than `context.md`, is shorthand for "the
corresponding path under `<output_dir>/<runs_subdir>/<run_id>/`" — substitute accordingly.
`context.md` is the one exception: it always lives directly under `<output_dir>/`, refreshed in
place, never inside a run folder.

When reading a prior stage's file and no `run_id` was set in config or stated by the user, use
the most recently modified run folder under `<output_dir>/<runs_subdir>/` instead of guessing —
and explicitly tell the user which run folder you read from.

## Inputs
- `output/test-plan.md` — must exist and should be human-reviewed/approved. Required.
- `output/context.md`, for terminology, module names, and environment details.
- `output/requirements.md` and `output/code-scan.md`, if present for this run — used to
  determine each test case's Origin (see Process).
- `output/rtm.md`, if present for this run — updated in place (see Process).
- `templates/test-case.template.md` — the required structure for each test case.

## Process
1. Work through `test-plan.md` scope area by area (not change by change — one scope area may
   need several test cases, one change may span several scope areas).
2. For each scope area, write test cases covering:
   - **Positive cases**: expected/happy-path behavior.
   - **Negative cases**: invalid input, unauthorized access, unexpected sequences, failure
     handling.
   - **Edge cases**: boundary values, empty/null/max states, race conditions, concurrency,
     timeouts — whatever is relevant to that specific area (not a generic boilerplate list).
3. Each test case must be independently executable: clear preconditions, numbered steps, and
   one unambiguous expected result per step or per case.
4. Assign a priority (High/Medium/Low) consistent with the risk rating from the test plan, and
   tag each case with the scope area / change it traces back to, for traceability.
5. **Classify each test case for fast review**:
   - **Origin**: `Requirement-based` if it traces to a CR/requirement ID in `output/requirements.md`
     for this run, otherwise `Implementation-based` if it traces to a `file:line` business rule in
     `output/code-scan.md`. If neither file exists or neither has a match, `Implementation-based`
     with the test plan's scope area as the traced source.
   - **Category** (pick the single best-fit bucket — use the Positive/Negative/Edge design work
     above to decide, then classify what the case is really checking): `Functional` (happy-path
     positive cases), `Regression` (re-verifying previously-working behavior near this change),
     `Boundary` (edge/limit values from the checklist above), `Negative` (invalid input,
     unauthorized access, failure handling not specifically security-related), `Security`
     (auth/authorization/injection/data-exposure concerns), or `Accessibility` (keyboard
     navigation, screen-reader labels, contrast/focus — wherever the scope area is user-facing UI).
   - **Automation Candidate**: `Yes` or `No`, with a one-line reason. Favor `Yes` for stable,
     deterministic, likely-to-be-repeated cases (regression, core functional, boundary checks on
     a stable API/form); favor `No` for exploratory, one-off, or judgment-heavy cases (visual
     review, ambiguous UX, anything needing human interpretation of "does this look right").
6. Group output by scope area, matching the test plan's structure, so a reviewer can cross-check
   plan coverage against test cases directly.
7. **CSV export**: write the test cases CSV (`test_cases_csv` path from config) alongside the
   markdown, unconditionally — this is a standing deliverable every run, not optional. One row
   per test case, columns: `Run ID, Scope Area, TC ID, Title, Origin, Category, Automation
   Candidate, Priority, Traces To, Preconditions, Steps, Expected Result`. This file is meant for
   the user to manually import into Google Sheets (File > Import > Append to current sheet)
   whenever they want it there — you do not touch Google Sheets or any external tool yourself.
8. **Update the RTM**: read `output/rtm.md` for this run IF it exists. For each test case whose
   Origin is `Requirement-based`, find that requirement's row and fill in `Test Case ID(s)`
   (append if the row already lists others) and set `Test Status` to "written, not yet executed."
   Never add a new row to the RTM here — rows originate only from requirements-analyzer;
   implementation-based test cases with no requirement ID simply don't touch the RTM.

## Rules
- Do not invent functionality that isn't described in the test plan or context. If you're
  unsure how a feature is supposed to behave, write the test case with an explicit
  "[ASSUMPTION: ...]" note rather than guessing silently.
- Keep steps concrete and tool-agnostic (a human executing this manually should be able to
  follow it without needing to read code).
- **Write every precondition, step, and expected result in real-user-behavior language** — what
  a user does and sees (clicks, inputs, screens, messages, outcomes) — never code identifiers,
  function/variable names, or internal implementation detail, even for Implementation-based
  cases traced from a code-scan.md rule.
- These are manual test cases for now — do not generate automation code.
- Do not modify any source file. You only write to `output/test-cases/`, the test cases CSV, and
  (updates only, never new rows) `output/rtm.md`/`rtm.csv`.

## Output
Write one markdown file per scope area under `output/test-cases/<scope-area-slug>.md`, each
following `templates/test-case.template.md`, AND the test cases CSV at the configured
`test_cases_csv` path — both every run, unconditionally. Report to the user how many test cases
were created broken down by Origin, by Category, and by Automation Candidate (Yes count), and
flag any assumptions made.

18	  reviewed and approved before test cases are written from it.

20	  write reports/docs under `output/`.
21	- **Single source of truth.** Each agent's real instructions live in one file under `prompts/`.
22	  The Claude Code agent/command files are generated from that one file, so you only ever edit a
23	  prompt in one place.
24	- **General-purpose.** Nothing here is hardcoded to a specific project, domain, or language.
25	  `context-analyzer` builds project-specific knowledge at runtime; every other agent reads that
26	  instead of assuming anything.
27	
28	## Requirements
29	
30	- [Claude Code](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code).
31	- Nothing else, for day-to-day use. `pyyaml` is only needed if you edit `prompts/` or
32	  `config/agents.yaml` and want to regenerate the agent files (`pip install pyyaml`).
33	
34	## Getting started
35	
36	1. Clone this repo into (or alongside) the project you want to test. If your target project is
37	   a separate repo, copy `.claude/`, `templates/`, and `output/` into it — or open Claude Code in
38	   your project directory and point it at this repo's `prompts/` and `templates/` via a relative
39	   path. Simplest: clone this repo *inside* the project repo (e.g. as `qa-pipeline/`) or as a
40	   sibling directory and `cd` into the project when invoking agents.
41	2. **Replace the bug report template.** `templates/bug-report.template.md` ships as a generic
42	   placeholder. Swap in your team's real template (Jira fields, internal tracker format,
43	   whatever you actually file against) before using `bug-reporter`.
44	3. Open Claude Code in your project.
45	4. Invoke agents explicitly, in order, reviewing output between stages (see workflow below).
46	
47	## Configuration
48	
49	`config/pipeline.config.yaml` controls where agents write their output: `output_dir` (default
50	`output`), `runs_subdir` (default `runs`), an optional `run_id`, plus the file/folder names
51	under each run. Every agent reads this file before writing anything and falls back to the same
52	defaults if it's missing, so deleting it is safe. Change `output_dir` if you want artifacts to
53	land somewhere other than `./output`, e.g. inside an existing `docs/` or `qa/` folder.
54	
55	**Run-versioned output.** Every stage's output lives under
56	`<output_dir>/<runs_subdir>/<run_id>/`, except `context.md`, which always lives directly at
57	`<output_dir>/context.md` — it's refreshed in place across cycles, not per-run, since it
58	describes the codebase rather than a specific release. `run_id` is resolved per invocation: the
59	value set in `config/pipeline.config.yaml`, or a run/release identifier you state in
60	conversation (e.g. a release tag or CR number), or — if neither is given — today's date
61	(`YYYY-MM-DD`). Every agent states which `run_id` it used at the top of its response, and if it
62	has to read a prior stage's file with no `run_id` given, it uses the most recently modified run
63	folder and tells you which one. Setting `run_id` explicitly is useful when you have concurrent
64	test cycles in flight (e.g. two release branches) and want their output kept cleanly separate.
65	
66	`config/pipeline.config.yaml` also has an `inputs:` block for optional input locations
67	(`requirements_docs`, `logs_dir`, `bug_template`) — leave these `null` and just point agents at
68	the right file in conversation if you'd rather not configure them.
69	
70	## Running the agents
71	
72	Open Claude Code in your project directory (`claude`), then either:
73	- **Ask directly:** `Use the context-analyzer subagent to analyze this codebase.`
74	- **@-mention it** (guarantees delegation instead of Claude deciding): `@context-analyzer analyze this codebase and update context.md`
75	- **List what's available:** `/agents`
76	
77	Agent names: `context-analyzer`, `changelog-analyzer`, `requirements-analyzer`, `code-scanner`,
78	`test-planner`, `test-case-writer`, `log-analyzer`, `rca-analyst`, `bug-reporter`,
79	`release-notes-writer`.
80	
81	## Running a pipeline (orchestrator)
82	
83	For running several stages back-to-back instead of one at a time, Claude Code gets a
84	`/qa-pipeline` slash command that chains the named stages in order:
85	
86	```
87	/qa-pipeline context changelog test-plan
88	/qa-pipeline requirements code-scan
89	/qa-pipeline test-cases
90	/qa-pipeline log-analysis
91	/qa-pipeline rca bug-report
92	/qa-pipeline release-notes
93	/qa-pipeline                          # no args = defaults to: context changelog test-plan
94	```
95	
96	All stages invoked in one `/qa-pipeline` call share the same `run_id` (see Configuration below)
97	— it's resolved once per invocation, not independently per stage.
98	
99	It still respects the human review gate: if you chain `test-plan` and `test-cases` together in
100	the same call, it deliberately stops after `test-plan` and asks you to review/approve before
101	you re-run it with just `test-cases`. It's a convenience for chaining stages you've already
102	decided on — it doesn't decide the plan for you, and it won't run a stage you didn't ask for.
103	
104	This is a command, not a 9th agent — it lives at `.claude/commands/qa-pipeline.md`, generated
105	from the source file at `prompts/commands/qa-pipeline.md`.
106	
107	## The agents
108	
109	| Order | Agent | Reads | Writes |
110	|---|---|---|---|
111	| 1 | `context-analyzer` | codebase | `output/context.md` |
112	| 2 | `changelog-analyzer` | changelog/commits/diff | `output/changes.md` |
113	| 3 | `requirements-analyzer` *(optional)* | SRS/CR doc, `changes.md`, `code-scan.md`\* | `output/requirements.md`, `output/rtm.md`, `output/rtm.csv` |
114	| 4 | `code-scanner` *(optional)* | changed code from `changes.md`, `context.md` | `output/code-scan.md` |
115	| 5 | `test-planner` | `changes.md`, `context.md`, `requirements.md`\*, `code-scan.md`\* | `output/test-plan.md`, `output/test-plan.csv` |
116	| — | *(human review & sign-off on the test plan)* | | |
117	| 6 | `test-case-writer` | `test-plan.md` | `output/test-cases/*.md`, `output/test-cases.csv`, updates `output/rtm.md`\* |
118	| 7 | `log-analyzer` | logs (ad hoc, during execution) | `output/log-analysis.md` |
119	| 8 | `rca-analyst` | bug symptom, code, logs, `changes.md` | `output/rca/*.md` |
120	| 9 | `bug-reporter` | RCA, test case, your template | `output/bugs/*.md`, updates `output/rtm.md`\* |
121	| 10 | `release-notes-writer` | everything above | `output/test-closure-report.md`, `output/release-notes.md` |
122	
123	\* read/updated only if present for the run — these are optional stages/artifacts and later
124	agents degrade gracefully (stating so explicitly) when they weren't run.
125	
126	`requirements-analyzer` is genuinely optional: it only does anything useful when an SRS/CR
127	document actually exists for the release. Point it at one, or skip the stage entirely — it will
128	say so plainly and stop rather than fabricate requirements if none is available.
129	
130	**Requirement Traceability Matrix (RTM).** `requirements-analyzer` seeds `output/rtm.md` +
131	`rtm.csv` (Requirement ID → Source Ref → Implementation Ref → Test Case ID(s) → Test Status →
132	Defect ID(s)) whenever it has a requirements document to extract from. `Implementation Ref` is
133	filled in from `code-scan.md`'s discovered business rules if that stage has already run this
134	cycle — run `code-scan` before `requirements` for a fuller RTM, though running `requirements`
135	first still works (that column just stays "pending"). `test-case-writer` and `bug-reporter` fill
136	in the remaining columns as the cycle progresses. If no requirements document exists, no RTM is
137	produced — same "say so plainly, don't fabricate" rule as `requirements.md` itself.
138	
139	`log-analyzer` and `rca-analyst` aren't strictly linear — use them whenever you're investigating
140	something, not only at a fixed point in the sequence.
141	
142	### CSV output
143	
144	`test-planner` and `test-case-writer` always write a CSV alongside their markdown
145	(`test-plan.csv`, `test-cases.csv`, paths configurable in `config/pipeline.config.yaml`) — no
146	setup required, this happens every run. They're meant for manual import into Google Sheets
147	(**File > Import > Append to current sheet**) whenever you want the data there; no agent in this
148	pipeline touches Google Sheets or any external tool itself.
149	
150	## Typical workflow
151	
152	```
153	# 1. Once per project (re-run after major structural changes)
154	Use the context-analyzer agent to analyze this codebase and produce context.md.
155	   -> writes directly to output/context.md, not run-versioned
156	
157	# 2. Every release — pick a run_id (or let it default to today's date)
158	Use the changelog-analyzer agent on the diff between <last-tag> and HEAD.
159	   -> writes output/runs/<run_id>/changes.md
160	
161	# 3. Optional, every release, after step 2
162	Use the requirements-analyzer agent against <SRS/CR doc> for this release.
163	Use the code-scanner agent to review the changed code from this run.
164	   -> writes output/runs/<run_id>/requirements.md and code-scan.md; skip either if not useful
165	      this cycle
166	
167	# 4. Every release, after step 2 (and step 3 if run)
168	Use the test-planner agent to produce a test plan for these changes.
169	   -> review output/runs/<run_id>/test-plan.md yourself, edit/approve it
170	   -> also writes test-plan.csv unconditionally (see CSV output note below)
171	
172	# 5. After the plan is approved
173	Use the test-case-writer agent to write test cases from the approved test plan.
174	   -> also writes test-cases.csv unconditionally
175	
176	# 6. During execution, as needed
177	Use the log-analyzer agent on <log file/path>.
178	Use the rca-analyst agent to investigate <symptom description>.
179	Use the bug-reporter agent to file a bug based on the RCA for <symptom>.
180	
181	# 7. At the end of the cycle
182	Use the release-notes-writer agent to prepare the closure report and release notes.
183	```
184	
185	Use the same `run_id` across a cycle (state it explicitly, e.g. "for run 2026-07-rc2") so every
186	stage's output lands in the same run folder — or just let every stage default to today's date if
187	you're not running concurrent cycles.
188	
189	Subagents are typically invoked by name (`@agent-name` or by asking Claude to "use the X agent").
190	
191	## Repo layout
192	
193	```
194	qa-agent-pipeline/
195	├── prompts/                 SOURCE OF TRUTH — one file per agent, plain instructions
196	│   └── commands/qa-pipeline.md  SOURCE OF TRUTH for the orchestrator command
197	├── config/
198	│   ├── agents.yaml           agent metadata (description, tool permissions)
199	│   ├── commands.yaml         command metadata (description, argument hint)
200	│   └── pipeline.config.yaml  where agents write output (output_dir + file names)
201	├── scripts/generate_agents.py   regenerates .claude/ from prompts/ + config/
202	├── .claude/agents/          generated — Claude Code subagent files (committed)
203	├── .claude/commands/        generated — Claude Code slash commands (committed)
204	├── templates/               required output structure for each agent
205	│   └── bug-report.template.md   <- replace this with your team's real template
206	├── output/                  where agents write results (gitignored per-project data,
207	│                             structure kept via .gitkeep; path configurable, see above)
208	├── dashboard/               optional local web UI — see dashboard/README.md
209	└── CHANGELOG.md             version history of this pipeline itself
210	```
211	
212	## Extending this
213	
214	To add a new agent (say, a performance-test analyzer):
215	1. Write `prompts/perf-analyzer.md` — the actual instructions, no frontmatter.
216	2. Add an entry to `config/agents.yaml` (id, description, tools).
217	3. Add an output template under `templates/` if it produces a new file type.
218	4. Run `python3 scripts/generate_agents.py`.
219	5. Commit everything, including the two generated agent files.
220	
221	To change an existing agent's behavior, edit its file under `prompts/` and re-run the generator
222	— never hand-edit files under `.claude/agents/` directly, they'll be overwritten next time
223	someone regenerates.
224	
225	Same pattern for commands: edit `prompts/commands/qa-pipeline.md` or `config/commands.yaml` to
226	change the orchestrator, or add a new `id` to `config/commands.yaml` plus a matching
227	`prompts/commands/<id>.md` for a new one, then re-run the generator.
228	
229	## Dashboard (optional)
230	
231	For a click-and-view alternative to typing agent invocations in Claude Code chat, there's a
232	local web dashboard under `dashboard/`: one button per agent, one button for the full
233	`/qa-pipeline` orchestrator, a live log of what's running, and a browser for the generated
234	`output/` files (rendered markdown, CSV as a table). It's a thin wrapper — every button shells
235	out to the exact same `claude` CLI invocations documented above — so the chat/CLI workflow keeps
236	working unchanged whether or not you use it.
237	
238	```
239	pip install -r dashboard/requirements.txt
240	python3 dashboard/server.py          # run from inside your project directory
241	```
242	
243	See `dashboard/README.md` for details, including how the test-plan review gate is surfaced in
244	the UI.
245	
246	## Versioning
247	
248	This pipeline is versioned independently of any project it's used in — see `VERSION` and
249	`CHANGELOG.md`. If you fork/customize this for your team, bump the version and log changes there
250	so improvements are traceable over time, same as any other codebase.
251

| Order | Agent | Reads | Writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `context-analyzer` | codebase | `output/context.md` |
| 2 | `changelog-analyzer` | changelog/commits/diff | `output/changes.md` |
| 3 | `requirements-analyzer` *(optional)* | SRS/CR doc, `changes.md`, `code-scan.md`\* | `output/requirements.md`, `output/rtm.md`, `output/rtm.csv` |
| 4 | `code-scanner` *(optional)* | changed code from `changes.md`, `context.md` | `output/code-scan.md` |
| 5 | `test-planner` | `changes.md`, `context.md`, `requirements.md`\*, `code-scan.md`\* | `output/test-plan.md`, `output/test-plan.csv` |
| — | *(human review & sign-off on the test plan)* | | |
| 6 | `test-case-writer` | `test-plan.md` | `output/test-cases/*.md`, `output/test-cases.csv`, updates `output/rtm.md`\* |
| 7 | `log-analyzer` | logs (ad hoc, during execution) | `output/log-analysis.md` |
| 8 | `rca-analyst` | bug symptom, code, logs, `changes.md` | `output/rca/*.md` |
| 9 | `bug-reporter` | RCA, test case, your template | `output/bugs/*.md`, updates `output/rtm.md`\* |
| 10 | `release-notes-writer` | everything above | `output/test-closure-report.md`, `output/release-notes.md` |

\* read/updated only if present for the run — these are optional stages/artifacts and later
agents degrade gracefully (stating so explicitly) when they weren't run.

`requirements-analyzer` is genuinely optional: it only does anything useful when an SRS/CR
document actually exists for the release. Point it at one, or skip the stage entirely — it will
say so plainly and stop rather than fabricate requirements if none is available.

**Requirement Traceability Matrix (RTM).** `requirements-analyzer` seeds `output/rtm.md` +
`rtm.csv` (Requirement ID → Source Ref → Implementation Ref → Test Case ID(s) → Test Status →
Defect ID(s)) whenever it has a requirements document to extract from. `Implementation Ref` is
filled in from `code-scan.md`'s discovered business rules if that stage has already run this
cycle — run `code-scan` before `requirements` for a fuller RTM, though running `requirements`
first still works (that column just stays "pending"). `test-case-writer` and `bug-reporter` fill
in the remaining columns as the cycle progresses. If no requirements document exists, no RTM is
produced — same "say so plainly, don't fabricate" rule as `requirements.md` itself.

`log-analyzer` and `rca-analyst` aren't strictly linear — use them whenever you're investigating
something, not only at a fixed point in the sequence.

### CSV output

`test-planner` and `test-case-writer` always write a CSV alongside their markdown
(`test-plan.csv`, `test-cases.csv`, paths configurable in `config/pipeline.config.yaml`) — no
setup required, this happens every run. They're meant for manual import into Google Sheets
(**File > Import > Append to current sheet**) whenever you want the data there; no agent in this
pipeline touches Google Sheets or any external tool itself.

## Typical workflow

```
# 1. Once per project (re-run after major structural changes)
Use the context-analyzer agent to analyze this codebase and produce context.md.
   -> writes directly to output/context.md, not run-versioned

# 2. Every release — pick a run_id (or let it default to today's date)
Use the changelog-analyzer agent on the diff between <last-tag> and HEAD.
   -> writes output/runs/<run_id>/changes.md

# 3. Optional, every release, after step 2
Use the requirements-analyzer agent against <SRS/CR doc> for this release.
Use the code-scanner agent to review the changed code from this run.
   -> writes output/runs/<run_id>/requirements.md and code-scan.md; skip either if not useful
      this cycle

# 4. Every release, after step 2 (and step 3 if run)
Use the test-planner agent to produce a test plan for these changes.
   -> review output/runs/<run_id>/test-plan.md yourself, edit/approve it
   -> also writes test-plan.csv unconditionally (see CSV output note below)

# 5. After the plan is approved
Use the test-case-writer agent to write test cases from the approved test plan.
   -> also writes test-cases.csv unconditionally

# 6. During execution, as needed
Use the log-analyzer agent on <log file/path>.
Use the rca-analyst agent to investigate <symptom description>.
Use the bug-reporter agent to file a bug based on the RCA for <symptom>.

# 7. At the end of the cycle
Use the release-notes-writer agent to prepare the closure report and release notes.
```

Use the same `run_id` across a cycle (state it explicitly, e.g. "for run 2026-07-rc2") so every
stage's output lands in the same run folder — or just let every stage default to today's date if
you're not running concurrent cycles.

Subagents are typically invoked by name (`@agent-name` or by asking Claude to "use the X agent").

## Repo layout

```
qa-agent-pipeline/
├── prompts/                 SOURCE OF TRUTH — one file per agent, plain instructions
│   └── commands/qa-pipeline.md  SOURCE OF TRUTH for the orchestrator command
├── config/
│   ├── agents.yaml           agent metadata (description, tool permissions)
│   ├── commands.yaml         command metadata (description, argument hint)
│   └── pipeline.config.yaml  where agents write output (output_dir + file names)
├── scripts/generate_agents.py   regenerates .claude/ from prompts/ + config/
├── .claude/agents/          generated — Claude Code subagent files (committed)
├── .claude/commands/        generated — Claude Code slash commands (committed)
├── templates/               required output structure for each agent
│   └── bug-report.template.md   <- replace this with your team's real template
├── output/                  where agents write results (gitignored per-project data,
│                             structure kept via .gitkeep; path configurable, see above)
├── dashboard/               optional local web UI — see dashboard/README.md
└── CHANGELOG.md             version history of this pipeline itself
```

## Extending this

To add a new agent (say, a performance-test analyzer):
1. Write `prompts/perf-analyzer.md` — the actual instructions, no frontmatter.
2. Add an entry to `config/agents.yaml` (id, description, tools).
3. Add an output template under `templates/` if it produces a new file type.
4. Run `python3 scripts/generate_agents.py`.
5. Commit everything, including the two generated agent files.

To change an existing agent's behavior, edit its file under `prompts/` and re-run the generator
— never hand-edit files under `.claude/agents/` directly, they'll be overwritten next time
someone regenerates.

Same pattern for commands: edit `prompts/commands/qa-pipeline.md` or `config/commands.yaml` to
change the orchestrator, or add a new `id` to `config/commands.yaml` plus a matching
`prompts/commands/<id>.md` for a new one, then re-run the generator.

## Dashboard (optional)

For a click-and-view alternative to typing agent invocations in Claude Code chat, there's a
local web dashboard under `dashboard/`: one button per agent, one button for the full
`/qa-pipeline` orchestrator, a live log of what's running, and a browser for the generated
`output/` files (rendered markdown, CSV as a table). It's a thin wrapper — every button shells
out to the exact same `claude` CLI invocations documented above — so the chat/CLI workflow keeps
working unchanged whether or not you use it.

```
pip install -r dashboard/requirements.txt
python3 dashboard/server.py          # run from inside your project directory
```

See `dashboard/README.md` for details, including how the test-plan review gate is surfaced in
the UI.

## Versioning

This pipeline is versioned independently of any project it's used in — see `VERSION` and
`CHANGELOG.md`. If you fork/customize this for your team, bump the version and log changes there
so improvements are traceable over time, same as any other codebase.

14	
15	## Overview
16	`rsc-service` ("Roaming Status Check API for M1", version `2.0.5`, `pom.xml`) is a telecom backend built for M1 Singapore. It checks whether a given MSISDN (mobile subscriber number) is currently roaming by querying the operator's HLR/VLR data through an SPML provisioning-gateway connector, caches results, logs transactions/events, and exposes reporting on those transactions through a separate web UI. It is a Maven multi-module project with three deployable modules: a reactive API service, a log/report data loader, and a Thymeleaf/Keycloak-secured report viewer (`pom.xml` `<modules>`).
17	
18	## Tech Stack
19	- **Language/runtime**: Kotlin 1.9.25 (main API + data loader), Java 21 (report viewer), JDK 21 target (`pom.xml` `java.version`).
20	- **Framework**: Spring Boot 3.5.6 (parent POM), Spring WebFlux + Kotlin coroutines (`rsc-service-api`), Spring MVC + Thymeleaf (`rsc-report-viewer`), Spring Data JDBC/JPA.
21	- **Build**: Maven, multi-module reactor (`rsc-service-parent`).
22	- **Key libraries**: `kotlinx-coroutines-reactor`, `resilience4j` (rate limiter, time limiter) for SPML call protection, `caffeine` (in-memory L1 cache), `mariadb-java-client`, `micrometer-tracing-bridge-brave` + `zipkin-reporter-brave` for distributed tracing, `hms-common-util` / `snmp-log-utils` (internal hSenid libraries for SNMP alarms), `spml-gw` (internal SPML connector library used to talk to the telecom provisioning gateway), Gson, `super-csv` (report export, confirmed in `rsc-report-viewer/pom.xml`), `mockk` / `mockito-kotlin` / `spring-boot-starter-test` / `reactor-test` for testing.
23	- **Data store**: MariaDB 11.4 (two logical DBs: `rsc_config_db` for users/config, `rsc_reporting_db`/`rsc-reporting` for transaction & event logs) — confirmed via `application.yml` datasource URLs and `data/config_db*`, `data/reporting_db*` Liquibase changelogs.
24	- **Auth**: `rsc-service-api` uses HTTP Basic-style `Authorization` header (base64 `user:password`) validated against a DB-backed user table (`VisitorAuthenticator.kt`). `rsc-report-viewer` uses OAuth2/OIDC login against Keycloak (`spring-boot-starter-oauth2-client`, `issuer-uri: https://localhost:8081/realms/rsc-report-viewer` — confirmed in `rsc-report-viewer/src/main/resources/application.yml`).
25	- **Infra**: Docker Compose files for local dev DB/infra and Liquibase migrations (`docker/docker-compose-*.yml`, `liquibase.sh`), HAProxy 2.6.0 mentioned as the fronting LB (Readme.md software versions list), RedHat 9.4 target OS.
26	
27	## Architecture
28	Monolith-ish multi-module system, not a single deployable — three independently built/deployed Spring Boot apps sharing the same MariaDB schemas and internal libraries:
29	
30	```
31	Roaming client (e.g. VPE/other operator)
32	      │ HTTPS + Basic Auth  (GET /vpe/api/visitorInfo/{version}/{msisdn})
33	      ▼
34	rsc-service-api (WebFlux, functional routers)
35	      │
36	      ├─ auth: VisitorAuthenticator ──► rsc_config_db (users/roles)
37	      ├─ workflow: WorkflowChain (chain-of-responsibility validators)
38	      │     NumberLengthValidator → NumberRangeValidator → CheckInCache →
39	      │     SpmlExistsValidator → SingleMsisdnRoamingValidator → MultiSimStatusValidator
40	      ├─ cache: DistributedMsisdnCacheManager — L1 Caffeine (per-instance) + L2 MariaDB
41	      │     (shared/distributed), background sync (30s) + cleanup (2min) schedulers
42	      ├─ connectors: SpmlConnectorAdapter → spml-gw library → SPML/XML provisioning
43	      │     gateway (HLR/VLR search + multi-SIM member check), rate-limited via resilience4j
44	      ├─ logs: TransLogger / EventLogger → transaction & event log tables/files
45	      └─ snmp: CommonSNMPManager → SNMP traps for DB errors, high TPS, timeouts, start/stop
46	
47	rsc-data-loader (Kotlin, scheduled batch/log processor)
48	      reads trans/event log files → parses via ColumnSpec/Transformers →
49	      writes to rsc_reporting_db (trans_log, tps_log, trx_events_log tables) →
50	      ReportGeneratorService produces summary/detail report tables
51	
52	rsc-report-viewer (Spring MVC + Thymeleaf, Keycloak OAuth2 login)
53	      ReportingController/ReportingService → DetailTransactionRepository (JPA/JDBC)
54	      → reads rsc_reporting_db → renders/downloads CSV reports (super-csv)
55	```
56	
57	## Modules / Components
58	- **rsc-service-api** — Reactive API that answers roaming-status lookups for MSISDNs against the telecom HLR/VLR via SPML, with caching, validation chain, auth, and alarms. Path: `rsc-service-api/src/main/kotlin/hms/core/m1/rsc/rscservice/`
59	  - `api/` — WebFlux functional route definitions (`RouteConfiguration.kt`) for `visitorInfo`, user management (`/user/add`, `/user/update-password`, `/user/change-status`), and cache admin (`/clear-cache`, `/clear-all-cache`).
60	  - `workflow/` — `WorkflowChain`/`WorkFlowStep` chain-of-responsibility pattern driving the roaming-check pipeline and building the response/cache entry.
61	  - `validator/` — individual chain steps: MSISDN length/range checks, SPML existence check, single-MSISDN roaming determination, multi-SIM status check, cache short-circuit (`CheckInCache`).
62	  - `connectors/` — `SpmlConnectorAdapter` wraps the internal `spml-gw` library to send XML SPML requests (`search_request.xml`, `multi_sim_member_check_request.xml`) and parse HLR/VLR/call-barring (odboc) XPath responses.
63	  - `cache/` — `DistributedMsisdnCacheManager` (hybrid L1 Caffeine + L2 MariaDB cache), `CacheRepository`, sync/cleanup schedulers.
64	  - `auth/` — Basic-auth style `VisitorAuthenticator`, DB-backed user repo/entity, `PasswordService`, `UserRoles` (ADMIN/USER).
65	  - `logs/` — `TransLogger`/`EventLogger`/TPS logger writing transaction, event, and TPS logs consumed later by `rsc-data-loader`.
66	  - `snmp/`, `alarms/` — SNMP trap alarms for DB errors, consecutive timeouts, high TPS, app start/stop.
67	  - `error/` — typed exceptions (`ApiErrorException`, `InternalErrorException`, `UnauthorizedException`, `ForbiddenException`, `DefaultErrorException`) mapped to HTTP statuses.
68	- **rsc-data-loader** — Batch/scheduled Kotlin service that parses trans/event/TPS log files and loads them into the reporting DB, then generates summary reports. Path: `rsc-data-loader/src/main/kotlin/hms/core/m1/rsc/dataloader/`
69	  - `logspecs/` — column specs and field `Transformer`s (`NullColumnTransformer`, `BooleanFieldTransformer`, `FieldWithColumnNameTransformer`) describing log file layouts.
70	  - `service/lineProcessor/`, `service/loadInFileProcessor/` — log line/file ingestion pipeline (`TransLogProcessor`, `LoadInFileProcessor`).
71	  - `service/reportGenerator/` — `ReportGeneratorService`/`ReportGeneratorRepository` builds summary/detail report tables.
72	  - `service/lock/` — `DistributedTemplateLockManager` (DB-based distributed locking, likely to keep multi-instance loaders from double-processing).
73	  - `snmp/` — SNMP alarm config mirroring the API module.
74	- **rsc-report-viewer** — Spring MVC web app (Java) with Keycloak SSO login for viewing/exporting roaming transaction reports. Path: `rsc-report-viewer/src/main/java/hms/core/m1/rsc/rscservice/viewer/`
75	  - `controller/` — `LoginController`, `ReportingController`.
76	  - `service/`, `service/impl/` — `ReportingService`/`ReportingServiceImpl`.
77	  - `repository/` — `DetailTransactionRepository`, `UserRepository` (JPA).
78	  - `configuration/` — `SecurityConfiguration`, `AuthoritiesConverter`, `CustomAuthenticationEvents` (Keycloak/OAuth2 role mapping).
79	  - `validator/` — `DetailTransactionReportValidator`, `DateFormatValidator` for report query params.
80	  - `health/` — `DbHealthChecker`.
81	  - `keycloak/theme/` — custom Keycloak login theme.
82	- **data/** — Liquibase changelogs for the four MariaDB schemas: `config_db`, `config_db_test`, `reporting_db`, `reporting_db_test`, plus `initial-data/` scripts (user seeding, `trx_events_log`/`trans_log`/`tps_log` partitioning). Path: `data/`
83	- **simulators/rsc-service-simulator/** — WireMock-based standalone simulator (jar + `mappings/`) used to fake SPML/downstream responses for testing (roaming true/false, unauthorized, bad-request, not-acceptable, internal-error scenarios). Path: `simulators/rsc-service-simulator/`
84	- **docs/** — HLD PlantUML/PNG diagrams (system context, API/report-viewer/data-loader component diagrams, deployment, DB designs) under `docs/hld/`, SRS/SOW/flow requirement docs under `docs/req/`, and real SPML XML/WSDL/XSD samples under `docs/spml_samples/`. Path: `docs/`
85	- **Documents/** — Untracked reference material (client-supplied SRS PDFs across versions `v0.0.2`–`v1.1.0`, SDP PDFs, SOW xlsx, flow/sequence diagrams, VPE OpenAPI spec, XSD/WSDL zips). Not code, useful background for requirements analysis. Path: `Documents/`
86	- **QA agent pipeline scaffold** (`config/`, `prompts/`, `templates/`, `output/`, `dashboard/`, `scripts/`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `VERSION`, root `README.md`) — this is tooling for the QA pipeline itself (this analysis run), not part of the deployed rsc-service product; confirmed untracked in `git status` in the target repo. Not a runtime component of the product under test.
87	
88	## Integration Points
89	- **SPML (XML over HTTP, via internal `spml-gw` connector library)** — outbound integration to the telecom Provisioning Gateway for HLR/VLR search (`search_request.xml`) and multi-SIM member check (`multi_sim_member_check_request.xml`); WSDL/XSD in `rsc-service-api/src/main/resources/spml/wsdl/` and `docs/spml_samples/`. Rate-limited to 50 req/s via `resilience4j` (`application.yml` `resilience4j.ratelimiter.instances.spml-requests`).
90	- **REST (Basic Auth) inbound API** — `rsc-service-api`, base path `/vpe/api` (`application.yml` `spring.webflux.base-path`): `GET /visitorInfo/{version}/{msisdn}`, `POST /user/add`, `PUT /user/update-password/{username}`, `PUT /user/change-status/{username}`, `DELETE /clear-cache/{msisdn}`, `GET /clear-all-cache` (`RouteConfiguration.kt`, lines 59/86/98/111/124/139 — re-verified this run, unchanged).
91	- **OAuth2/OIDC via Keycloak** — `rsc-report-viewer` login, issuer `https://localhost:8081/realms/rsc-report-viewer` (dev config; confirm prod issuer separately — not confirmed).
92	- **MariaDB** — shared L2 cache table + config/user data (`rsc_config_db`) for `rsc-service-api`; transaction/event/summary report tables (`rsc_reporting_db`) written by `rsc-data-loader` and read by `rsc-report-viewer`. Connection via `mariadb-java-client` + HikariCP.
93	- **SNMP traps** — `CommonSNMPManager` (internal `snmp-log-utils` lib) sends traps for DB errors, consecutive timeouts, high TPS, and app start/stop, via a configured shell script (`service-api.snmp.snmp-file-path: /hms/scripts/sample_snmp.sh`).
94	- **Distributed tracing** — Brave/Zipkin via Micrometer Tracing (`micrometer-tracing-bridge-brave`), trace ID surfaced in logs and as `X-Trace-Id`-style context (`Context.traceId`).
95	- **Liquibase** — schema migration/versioning for all four MariaDB schemas (`liquibase.sh`, `data/*/changelog`, `docker/docker-compose-db-migrate-*.yml`).
96	
97	## Test Conventions
98	- **Framework**: JUnit 5 via `spring-boot-starter-test`, `mockk` (Kotlin-idiomatic mocking) and `mockito-kotlin` as mocking libraries, `reactor-test` for WebFlux/coroutine flows. Report viewer additionally uses `spring-security-test` and `kotlin-test`.

Last updated: 2026-08-31 — refresh (run_id `2026-08-31`), output relocated to configured
`output_dir` = `/hms/projects/m1_rsc/rsc108/rsc-service-qa-pipeline` per explicit user

pipeline default would otherwise have been `./output` inside `rsc-service/`; a prior copy of
this file exists there and was used as the baseline for this refresh). Re-verified against the
current working tree (`git log -1` still `2828ad6` / tag `2.0.5`, `git status --short` shows only
the untracked QA-pipeline scaffold files — no product source changes, `git diff HEAD --stat`
empty). Spot-re-checked this run: `pom.xml` version/module list, `RouteConfiguration.kt` route
list, `application.yml` keys, absence of CI config, `super-csv` dependency in
`rsc-report-viewer/pom.xml`, Keycloak `issuer-uri`, and presence of the checked-in `.p12`/`.jks`
keystores. All prior claims held; no corrections needed this cycle.

## Overview
`rsc-service` ("Roaming Status Check API for M1", version `2.0.5`, `pom.xml`) is a telecom backend built for M1 Singapore. It checks whether a given MSISDN (mobile subscriber number) is currently roaming by querying the operator's HLR/VLR data through an SPML provisioning-gateway connector, caches results, logs transactions/events, and exposes reporting on those transactions through a separate web UI. It is a Maven multi-module project with three deployable modules: a reactive API service, a log/report data loader, and a Thymeleaf/Keycloak-secured report viewer (`pom.xml` `<modules>`).

## Tech Stack
- **Language/runtime**: Kotlin 1.9.25 (main API + data loader), Java 21 (report viewer), JDK 21 target (`pom.xml` `java.version`).
- **Framework**: Spring Boot 3.5.6 (parent POM), Spring WebFlux + Kotlin coroutines (`rsc-service-api`), Spring MVC + Thymeleaf (`rsc-report-viewer`), Spring Data JDBC/JPA.
- **Build**: Maven, multi-module reactor (`rsc-service-parent`).
- **Key libraries**: `kotlinx-coroutines-reactor`, `resilience4j` (rate limiter, time limiter) for SPML call protection, `caffeine` (in-memory L1 cache), `mariadb-java-client`, `micrometer-tracing-bridge-brave` + `zipkin-reporter-brave` for distributed tracing, `hms-common-util` / `snmp-log-utils` (internal hSenid libraries for SNMP alarms), `spml-gw` (internal SPML connector library used to talk to the telecom provisioning gateway), Gson, `super-csv` (report export, confirmed in `rsc-report-viewer/pom.xml`), `mockk` / `mockito-kotlin` / `spring-boot-starter-test` / `reactor-test` for testing.
- **Data store**: MariaDB 11.4 (two logical DBs: `rsc_config_db` for users/config, `rsc_reporting_db`/`rsc-reporting` for transaction & event logs) — confirmed via `application.yml` datasource URLs and `data/config_db*`, `data/reporting_db*` Liquibase changelogs.
- **Auth**: `rsc-service-api` uses HTTP Basic-style `Authorization` header (base64 `user:password`) validated against a DB-backed user table (`VisitorAuthenticator.kt`). `rsc-report-viewer` uses OAuth2/OIDC login against Keycloak (`spring-boot-starter-oauth2-client`, `issuer-uri: https://localhost:8081/realms/rsc-report-viewer` — confirmed in `rsc-report-viewer/src/main/resources/application.yml`).
- **Infra**: Docker Compose files for local dev DB/infra and Liquibase migrations (`docker/docker-compose-*.yml`, `liquibase.sh`), HAProxy 2.6.0 mentioned as the fronting LB (Readme.md software versions list), RedHat 9.4 target OS.

## Architecture
Monolith-ish multi-module system, not a single deployable — three independently built/deployed Spring Boot apps sharing the same MariaDB schemas and internal libraries:

```
Roaming client (e.g. VPE/other operator)
      │ HTTPS + Basic Auth  (GET /vpe/api/visitorInfo/{version}/{msisdn})
      ▼
rsc-service-api (WebFlux, functional routers)
      │
      ├─ auth: VisitorAuthenticator ──► rsc_config_db (users/roles)
      ├─ workflow: WorkflowChain (chain-of-responsibility validators)
      │     NumberLengthValidator → NumberRangeValidator → CheckInCache →
      │     SpmlExistsValidator → SingleMsisdnRoamingValidator → MultiSimStatusValidator
      ├─ cache: DistributedMsisdnCacheManager — L1 Caffeine (per-instance) + L2 MariaDB
      │     (shared/distributed), background sync (30s) + cleanup (2min) schedulers
      ├─ connectors: SpmlConnectorAdapter → spml-gw library → SPML/XML provisioning
      │     gateway (HLR/VLR search + multi-SIM member check), rate-limited via resilience4j
      ├─ logs: TransLogger / EventLogger → transaction & event log tables/files
      └─ snmp: CommonSNMPManager → SNMP traps for DB errors, high TPS, timeouts, start/stop

rsc-data-loader (Kotlin, scheduled batch/log processor)
      reads trans/event log files → parses via ColumnSpec/Transformers →
      writes to rsc_reporting_db (trans_log, tps_log, trx_events_log tables) →
      ReportGeneratorService produces summary/detail report tables

rsc-report-viewer (Spring MVC + Thymeleaf, Keycloak OAuth2 login)
      ReportingController/ReportingService → DetailTransactionRepository (JPA/JDBC)
      → reads rsc_reporting_db → renders/downloads CSV reports (super-csv)
```

## Modules / Components
- **rsc-service-api** — Reactive API that answers roaming-status lookups for MSISDNs against the telecom HLR/VLR via SPML, with caching, validation chain, auth, and alarms. Path: `rsc-service-api/src/main/kotlin/hms/core/m1/rsc/rscservice/`
  - `api/` — WebFlux functional route definitions (`RouteConfiguration.kt`) for `visitorInfo`, user management (`/user/add`, `/user/update-password`, `/user/change-status`), and cache admin (`/clear-cache`, `/clear-all-cache`).
  - `workflow/` — `WorkflowChain`/`WorkFlowStep` chain-of-responsibility pattern driving the roaming-check pipeline and building the response/cache entry.
  - `validator/` — individual chain steps: MSISDN length/range checks, SPML existence check, single-MSISDN roaming determination, multi-SIM status check, cache short-circuit (`CheckInCache`).
  - `connectors/` — `SpmlConnectorAdapter` wraps the internal `spml-gw` library to send XML SPML requests (`search_request.xml`, `multi_sim_member_check_request.xml`) and parse HLR/VLR/call-barring (odboc) XPath responses.
  - `cache/` — `DistributedMsisdnCacheManager` (hybrid L1 Caffeine + L2 MariaDB cache), `CacheRepository`, sync/cleanup schedulers.
  - `auth/` — Basic-auth style `VisitorAuthenticator`, DB-backed user repo/entity, `PasswordService`, `UserRoles` (ADMIN/USER).
  - `logs/` — `TransLogger`/`EventLogger`/TPS logger writing transaction, event, and TPS logs consumed later by `rsc-data-loader`.
  - `snmp/`, `alarms/` — SNMP trap alarms for DB errors, consecutive timeouts, high TPS, app start/stop.
  - `error/` — typed exceptions (`ApiErrorException`, `InternalErrorException`, `UnauthorizedException`, `ForbiddenException`, `DefaultErrorException`) mapped to HTTP statuses.
- **rsc-data-loader** — Batch/scheduled Kotlin service that parses trans/event/TPS log files and loads them into the reporting DB, then generates summary reports. Path: `rsc-data-loader/src/main/kotlin/hms/core/m1/rsc/dataloader/`
  - `logspecs/` — column specs and field `Transformer`s (`NullColumnTransformer`, `BooleanFieldTransformer`, `FieldWithColumnNameTransformer`) describing log file layouts.
  - `service/lineProcessor/`, `service/loadInFileProcessor/` — log line/file ingestion pipeline (`TransLogProcessor`, `LoadInFileProcessor`).
  - `service/reportGenerator/` — `ReportGeneratorService`/`ReportGeneratorRepository` builds summary/detail report tables.
  - `service/lock/` — `DistributedTemplateLockManager` (DB-based distributed locking, likely to keep multi-instance loaders from double-processing).

# Test Plan — rsc-service, release train through `2.0.5`/`3.0.5` (run `2026-08-31`)

Based on: `output/changes.md`, `output/context.md`, `output/requirements.md`, `output/code-scan.md`
(all read from `/hms/projects/m1_rsc/rsc108/rsc-service-qa-pipeline/runs/2026-08-31/` and
`/hms/projects/m1_rsc/rsc108/rsc-service-qa-pipeline/context.md` for this run_id — all four
existed for this run, so all were used).
Status: DRAFT — requires human review and sign-off before test case writing begins

**Config note**: no `config/pipeline.config.yaml` was found in the target project
(`rsc-service`'s own `config/` directory does not contain this pipeline's config — consistent
with `context.md`'s note for this run that no such file exists there). Per explicit user
instruction for this session, `output_dir` = `/hms/projects/m1_rsc/rsc108/rsc-service-qa-pipeline`
and `run_id` = `2026-08-31` were used directly, overriding any pipeline default. No `test_plan_csv`
path was configured (no config file to read one from), so the CSV was written alongside this file
as `test-plan.csv`, following the naming convention already established by this run's other
artifacts (`rtm.md`/`rtm.csv`).

## Scope Summary
This release train spans two eras: a 2022–2023 original build-out and an active 2025–2026
relaunch (`2.0.0`→`2.0.5`/`3.0.5`) that upgraded the whole stack to JDK 21/Spring Boot 3.5.6,
replaced Hazelcast with a MariaDB+Caffeine hybrid cache and MariaDB-based distributed locking,
replaced the report viewer's login with Keycloak OAuth2/OIDC, exposed Spring Actuator on both
web-facing modules, upgraded MariaDB itself (10.6.8→11.4), and most recently corrected the
cache's country-based TTL logic (the freshest product commit in the repo). Several legacy-era
changes are still live in the shipped `2.0.5` codebase and materially affect current testing: an
API response-contract change (not-found/invalid MSISDN now returns `HTTP 200`/`roaming:false`
instead of an error status) and unsalted MD5 password hashing for API user accounts. The overall
testing approach prioritizes the cache subsystem (highest churn, most recent change, two
code-scan Should-Fix findings), authentication/session boundaries (two different auth models,
one just swapped entirely), and the two code-scan Blocker-severity unauthenticated Actuator
exposures, before moving to lower-risk config/infra tuning and legacy-but-still-live contract
behavior. Legacy-era, long-shipped changes with zero code touched this release (SNMP alarms,
report-generation internals, routing, DB-migration script logic) are called out as advisory
"known fragile, not tested this cycle" rather than pulled into scope.

## Impacted Areas

### 1. Hybrid L1/L2 MSISDN Cache Subsystem (`rsc-service-api`)
- **Traces to change(s):** Breaking Change "Hazelcast removed, Caffeine+MariaDB hybrid cache"
  (`97491d5`, `54b64d6`, `e569ef5`, `d1b1a33`, `b82c39a`, `e040a85`, `b1c0bf2`, `e417512`,
  `fddf8fb`, `3b993ef`, `8d61853`); New Feature "Hybrid L1/L2 cache" (`e040a85` et al.);
  Enhancement "Cache TTL-by-VLR logic corrected" (`5c0d862`, most recent product commit);
  Enhancement "TTL unit configuration added" (`6a3d468`); Enhancement "scheduler interval
  tuning" (`e5e9fdb`); Bug Fix "concurrent cache-eviction issue" (`e55f7a0`)
- **Impact type:** Direct
- **Risk:** High — **code complexity**: full architecture swap plus a just-corrected TTL bug,
  touching `DistributedMsisdnCacheManager`, `CacheRepositoryImpl`, `CacheSyncScheduler`,
  `CacheCleanupScheduler`, `CacheConfiguration`; **business impact**: this is the core
  performance/correctness path for every roaming lookup (blast radius = all `visitorInfo`
  traffic); **data sensitivity**: caches roaming status tied to MSISDN (subscriber-identifying
  data); **module dependencies**: `WorkflowChain`/`CheckInCache` validator step and
  `clear-cache`/`clear-all-cache` admin endpoints depend on this subsystem, per `context.md`.
  Reweighted further toward High by `code-scan.md` Should-Fix findings: (1) the documented
  "degraded mode" fallback (L2 write failure → L1-only entry) is evicted by the next 30s sync
  cycle instead of surviving, defeating its purpose (`DistributedMsisdnCacheManager.kt:74-89`,
  `CacheSyncScheduler.kt:94-99`); (2) dead/commented-out code left in the just-rewritten
  `isNeighbouringMsisdn` function (`DistributedMsisdnCacheManager.kt:241`); plus a Note that L1
  (Caffeine) has no per-entry TTL, so neighbouring-country entries can be served up to 120 extra
  minutes past their intended window if the sync scheduler lags (`CacheConfiguration.kt:44,49-51`).
  Also reweighted by the churn/defect heuristic: `DistributedMsisdnCacheManager.kt` and
  `CacheSyncScheduler.kt` were each touched 3-4 separate times within this single ~3-month
  release window (`git log --stat`, 2025-10 to 2026-01) — high change density in a short window,
  corroborating (not primary) evidence given the guardrail on short windows.
- **Test scope:** Functional (cache hit/miss, TTL-by-VLR for neighbouring vs. non-neighbouring
  countries, multi-SIM member caching), integration (L1↔L2 sync every 30s, cleanup every 2min,
  multi-instance staleness window), regression (concurrent add/evict race — code-scan notes the
  "fix" may not have closed the race), negative (MariaDB outage → degraded-mode behavior and its
  ~30s eviction), performance (behavior under the 50 TPS SPML rate limit with cache miss storms).
- **Notes:** The graceful-degradation and L1/L2 TTL-mismatch behaviors documented above are
  **possible impact, needs verification** as to whether they are accepted risk or genuine defects
  — see Open Questions.

### 2. MariaDB-based Distributed Locking (`rsc-data-loader`)
- **Traces to change(s):** Breaking Change / New Feature "Hazelcast locks replaced with
  MariaDB-based distributed locking" (`97491d5`); Enhancement "Node ID removed from
  distributed-lock logs" (`796660b`)
- **Impact type:** Direct
- **Risk:** High — **code complexity**: full reimplementation of `DistributedTemplateLockManager`
  (old Hazelcast-based class deleted, new MariaDB-based class added, ~110 new lines);
  **business impact**: this lock prevents multi-instance `rsc-data-loader` deployments from
  double-processing the same trans/event/TPS log files — a failure here causes duplicate or
  lost reporting data; **data sensitivity**: indirectly (protects integrity of the reporting
  data pipeline); **module dependencies**: `ReportGeneratorService` runs under this lock, per
  `context.md`. Reweighted toward High by the churn/defect heuristic: `changes.md`'s legacy
  consolidated bug-fix theme (`0.0.2`–`1.0.8`, tracked bug IDs 46025–46560, "dozens of commits")
  explicitly includes "dangling distributed-lock cleanup on restart" as a historically recurring
  defect category in the *predecessor* locking mechanism — the same functional risk (locks not
  released cleanly) now applies to a brand-new implementation with presumably less production
  soak time.
- **Test scope:** Functional (lock acquire/release under normal operation), integration
  (multi-instance `rsc-data-loader` contention for the same log file), negative (lock holder
  crash/restart mid-processing — does the lock get cleaned up, given the historical "dangling
  lock" defect pattern in the old implementation?), regression (single-instance behavior
  unchanged post-migration).
- **Notes:** No unit/integration test evidence was found for the crash/restart-cleanup scenario
  specifically — **possible impact, needs verification**.

### 3. `rsc-report-viewer` Login & Session (Keycloak OAuth2/OIDC)
- **Traces to change(s):** Breaking Change "login mechanism replaced with Keycloak OAuth2/OIDC"
  (`33aa81d`, `8085764`, `d89ae70`, `6e75246`, `318c77f`)
- **Impact type:** Direct
- **Risk:** High — **code complexity**: full rewrite of `SecurityConfiguration`/
  `LoginController`, new `KeycloakUtil`/`AuthoritiesConverter` role mapping, new login theme;
  **business impact**: this is the only entry point to the reporting UI — a login regression
  blocks all reporting access; **data sensitivity**: authentication/session handling, directly
  auth-boundary code; **module dependencies**: every screen under `/reporting/**` depends on this
  boundary (see Area 4). Confirmed still High by `code-scan.md` Should-Fix: the previous explicit
  `.requestMatchers("/reporting/**").hasAnyRole("ADMIN","USER")` rule was replaced with a blanket
  `.anyRequest().authenticated()` — any authenticated user, regardless of role, can now reach
  every reporting screen and CSV download (`SecurityConfiguration.java:72-75`).
- **Test scope:** Functional (login success/failure via Keycloak, logout — code-scan confirms
  logout now redirects through a Keycloak end-session URL, ending SSO session not just local
  session), security (role/authorization testing — confirm whether ADMIN vs. USER distinction is
  still enforced anywhere, given the blanket-authenticated rule), negative (expired/invalid
  token, Keycloak unreachable), regression (session behavior compared to the prior local-login
  flow — SSL support was also added to this module in the same era, worth confirming interaction).
- **Notes:** Whether role-gating loss is intentional is a genuine open question — see Open
  Questions. Production Keycloak issuer/realm config is unconfirmed (`context.md` "Not
  Confirmed") — **possible impact, needs verification** for any environment-specific auth
  behavior beyond the `localhost:8081` dev config.

### 4. Reporting Screens, Access Control & CSV Downloads (`rsc-report-viewer`)
- **Traces to change(s):** Ripple from Area 3 (role-gating removal now applies to all
  `/reporting/**` routes); Bug Fix "TPS report CSV not downloading" (`599ce75`); Bug Fix "typo in
  `messages_en.properties`" (`da989dc`)
- **Impact type:** Ripple (from Area 3) + Direct (TPS download fix, typo fix)
- **Risk:** High — **code complexity**: low for the fixes themselves (one template path
  correction, one string fix), but **business impact** is high because the access-control change
  from Area 3 applies uniformly to detail-transaction, daily-transaction-summary,
  daily-status-analysis, and tps-utilization screens — a role-gating regression here affects all
  four report types; **data sensitivity**: transaction/roaming reports contain MSISDN/IMSI data;
  **module dependencies**: `ReportingController`/`ReportingService` read from `rsc_reporting_db`,
  populated by Area 6's log pipeline. `code-scan.md` confirms the download-path fix is now
  consistent across all three affected templates (`tps-utilization.html:168`,
  `daily-status-analysis.html:163`, `daily-transaction-summary.html:168`), matching
  `ReportingController`'s actual mapping.
- **Test scope:** Functional (all four report types render/filter/paginate correctly), regression
  (CSV download works for all report types, not just TPS — the fix confirms 3 templates were
  affected, worth confirming `detail-transaction.html` was never broken the same way), security
  (verify who can now reach these screens post role-gating removal), negative (empty result sets,
  invalid date-range filters).
- **Notes:** none.

### 5. Spring Actuator Exposure (`rsc-service-api` + `rsc-report-viewer`)
- **Traces to change(s):** Breaking Change "Spring Actuator exposed on both modules... `/actuator`,
  `/actuator/**` explicitly `permitAll()`" (`d89ae70`)
- **Impact type:** Direct
- **Risk:** High — **code complexity**: low (configuration-only change); **business impact**:
  very high — unauthenticated access to operational internals on two public-facing modules;
  **data sensitivity**: high — env vars, datasource URL/credentials, heap dumps reachable
  unauthenticated; **module dependencies**: n/a (this is an exposure surface, not a functional
  dependency). Confirmed High by two `code-scan.md` Blockers: (1) `rsc-service-api` has *no*
  Spring Security dependency at all, so every actuator endpoint including `/env`, `/heapdump`,
  `/threaddump`, `/beans`, `/mappings` is reachable by anyone with network access
  (`application.yml:30-44`), compounded by plaintext default DB/keystore passwords
  (`password`) committed in the same file; (2) `rsc-report-viewer` has Spring Security available
  but explicitly `permitAll()`s `/actuator/**` anyway (`SecurityConfiguration.java:73`).
- **Test scope:** Security (attempt unauthenticated access to `/actuator/env`, `/actuator/heapdump`,
  `/actuator/threaddump`, `/actuator/beans`, `/actuator/mappings` on both modules — confirm
  whether findable and whether they leak credentials), functional (confirm `db`/`diskspace`
  health indicators work as intended for legitimate monitoring use), negative (confirm default
  credentials in `application.yml` are overridden in the target test/prod environment before
  relying on this not being exploitable there).
- **Notes:** This is a security posture question as much as a test scope item — whether this
  exposure is acceptable for any given environment is a release-owner decision, not a QA call;
  flagged for explicit sign-off in Entry Criteria.

### 6. MSISDN Validation / API Response Contract (`rsc-service-api`)
- **Traces to change(s):** Breaking Change (legacy, still live) "API response contract change:
  invalid/not-found MSISDN returns `HTTP 200`/`roaming:false` instead of `4xx`" (`c94f4ab`,
  `62302ca`, release `1.0.5`)
- **Impact type:** Direct (legacy change, confirmed still shipped in current `2.0.5` per
  `code-scan.md`'s independent code review)
- **Risk:** High — **code complexity**: low (validator-level behavior, confirmed in
  `NumberLengthValidator.kt:37-40`, `NumberRangeValidator.kt:42-49`, `SpmlExistsValidator.kt:30-34`
  per `code-scan.md`'s "Business Rules & Behavior Discovered"); **business impact**: high —
  every external consumer ("VPE"/other operators, per `context.md`) that checks HTTP status
  rather than the `roaming` field to detect "not found" cannot distinguish "confirmed not
  roaming" from "invalid number" from "number not found" — all three look identical on the wire;
  **data sensitivity**: roaming status is the product's core data output; **module
  dependencies**: this is the primary inbound API contract, consumed externally (exact consumer
  list is "not confirmed" per `context.md`). This directly conflicts with SRS requirement
  `REQ-SDP-RSC 10.1` (documents `HTTP 406 Not Acceptable` for not-found) — see CR Traceability
  and Open Questions.
- **Test scope:** Functional (valid/invalid/not-found MSISDN response bodies and status codes),
  regression (confirm this behavior is consistent across the whole validation chain — length,
  range, and SPML-not-found cases all converge to the same `200`/`roaming:false` response),
  negative (malformed MSISDN, missing IMSI), contract/consumer-impact testing if any known
  consumer can be identified to check status-code-based branching.
- **Notes:** Whether this is the intended, accepted contract (superseding the SRS) is a genuine
  open question — see Open Questions.

### 7. Basic-Auth Password Hashing / User Management (`rsc-service-api`)
- **Traces to change(s):** Breaking Change (legacy, still live) "Password authentication
  converted to MD5 hashing" (`4f29b14`, `a27b73a`, release `0.0.4`)
- **Impact type:** Direct (legacy change, confirmed still shipped in current `2.0.5` per
  `code-scan.md`)
- **Risk:** High — **code complexity**: low; **business impact**: high — this protects
  `/user/add`, `/user/update-password`, `/user/change-status` and the Basic-Auth credential
  check itself; **data sensitivity**: very high — user credentials; **module dependencies**:
  `VisitorAuthenticator` and the DB-backed user table depend on `PasswordService`, per
  `context.md`. Confirmed High by `code-scan.md` Should-Fix: passwords are hashed with plain
  unsalted MD5 (`PasswordService.kt:22-26`), cryptographically broken and trivially reversible
  via rainbow tables for non-unique passwords.
- **Test scope:** Security (password storage review — no new test coverage will "fix" this, but
  regression tests should confirm current login/auth behavior so any future remediation doesn't
  break auth), functional (add user / update password / change status flows), negative
  (duplicate/weak passwords, since there's no policy enforcement visible in this hashing scheme).

37	
38	- **`rsc-report-viewer/.../configuration/SecurityConfiguration.java:72-75`** — The explicit
39	  `.requestMatchers("/reporting/**").hasAnyRole("ADMIN", "USER")` rule was removed and replaced
40	  with a blanket `.anyRequest().authenticated()`. Any user who successfully logs in via Keycloak
41	  — regardless of which realm role (if any) they hold — can now reach every `/reporting/**`
42	  screen and CSV download. Before this release, only users with the `ADMIN` or `USER` realm role
43	  could. If role-gating of report access is still an intended business rule, it is silently gone;
44	  worth confirming with the release owner whether this is intentional. Related change: Breaking
45	  Changes / Keycloak login replacement (`33aa81d`, `d89ae70`).
46	- **`rsc-service-api/.../cache/DistributedMsisdnCacheManager.kt:74-89`** and
47	  **`rsc-service-api/.../cache/scheduler/CacheSyncScheduler.kt:94-99`** — The documented
48	  "graceful degradation" path (a comment states: "If L2 write fails, still updates L1 (degraded
49	  mode)... for temporary availability") doesn't actually survive past the next sync cycle. When a
50	  MariaDB write fails, the entry is added to the in-memory (L1) cache only and never reaches the
51	  database. The sync job (`CacheSyncScheduler`, default every 30 seconds per
52	  `application.yml`) computes `keysToDelete = currentL1Keys - l2Keys` and evicts anything present
53	  in L1 but absent from the database — which includes the exact entries that were just added in
54	  degraded mode. In practice, an entry meant to give "temporary availability" during a DB outage
55	  is wiped from the in-memory cache within about 30 seconds instead of surviving until its
56	  intended TTL (120 or 240 minutes), defeating the purpose of the fallback. Related change: New
57	  Feature / hybrid L1/L2 cache (`e040a85`, `b82c39a`), Bug Fix / concurrent cache-eviction fix
58	  (`e55f7a0`).

60	  commented-out copy of the `isNeighbouringMsisdn` function was left in the file when it was
61	  rewritten in the same commit that changed its behavior (splitting `vlrAddress` on commas and
62	  checking each VLR individually instead of matching the whole string). Dead/commented-out code
63	  left in a file that was specifically touched to fix a caching bug. Related change: Enhancements
64	  / "Cache TTL-by-VLR logic corrected" (`5c0d862`).
65	- **`rsc-service-api/.../auth/credentials/PasswordService.kt:22-26`** — User passwords for the
66	  `rsc-service-api` Basic-Auth login (`/user/add`, `/user/update-password`) are hashed with plain
67	  unsalted MD5 (`MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5")`, no salt/pepper, no iteration/stretching).
68	  MD5 is cryptographically broken for this purpose and, without a salt, is trivially reversible
69	  via rainbow tables for any password not already unique per-user. This is long-standing (2022)
70	  but is still the live authentication mechanism for the currently shipped `2.0.5` API and is
71	  explicitly in the reviewed changes ("Password authentication converted to MD5 hashing").

108	  no longer returns an error status. It returns `HTTP 200` with body `{"roaming": false}`, exactly
109	  as if the number were confirmed not roaming.
110	- **`rsc-service-api/.../validator/NumberRangeValidator.kt:42-49`** — Same behavior for numbers
111	  that don't match any of the configured allowed prefixes (`service-api.msisdn-validations.range`,
112	  e.g. `^658\d*,^659\d*`): `HTTP 200`, `{"roaming": false}`, no error.
113	- **`rsc-service-api/.../validator/SpmlExistsValidator.kt:30-34`** — If the HLR/VLR lookup (SPML)
114	  reports the MSISDN doesn't exist at all, the user again gets `HTTP 200`, `{"roaming": false}`
115	  rather than a not-found/not-acceptable error. Any consumer that branches on HTTP status instead
116	  of reading the `roaming` field will not be able to distinguish "confirmed not roaming" from
117	  "invalid number" from "number not found" — all three look identical on the wire.
118	- **`rsc-service-api/.../cache/DistributedMsisdnCacheManager.kt:243-255`,

122	  (default regex `^659\d*`), the entry is cached for the shorter "neighbouring" window (120
123	  minutes default); otherwise it gets the longer "non-neighbouring" window (240 minutes default).
124	  For multi-SIM numbers, each member's own VLR address is checked individually.
125	- **`rsc-service-api/.../workflow/WorkflowChain.kt:125-126`** — Only responses where
126	  `roamingStatus == true` are ever written to the cache; "not roaming" and invalid/not-found
127	  results (see above) are never cached and will always trigger a fresh SPML lookup on the next
128	  request for that MSISDN.
129	- **`rsc-service-api/.../cache/DistributedMsisdnCacheManager.kt:74-89,122-149`** — Cache reads and
130	  writes degrade gracefully around MariaDB outages rather than failing the request: a failed L2
131	  write still updates the in-memory L1 cache (see Should-Fix above for the caveat that this
132	  doesn't last), and a failed L2 read is treated as a cache miss (returns `null`), which forces a
133	  live SPML/HLR lookup for that request instead of an error.
134	- **`rsc-service-api/src/main/resources/application.yml:105-116`** (per `e5e9fdb`) — L1/L2 cache
135	  sync between instances runs every 30 seconds (30s initial delay), and expired-row cleanup in
136	  MariaDB runs every 2 minutes. Multi-instance deployments should expect up to ~30s of
137	  cross-instance cache staleness by design.
138	- **`rsc-report-viewer/.../configuration/SecurityConfiguration.java:59-90`,
139	  `util/KeycloakUtil.java:16-24`** — Login now goes through Keycloak OAuth2/OIDC instead of a
140	  local username/password form; on logout, the app builds a Keycloak end-session URL using the
141	  user's ID token and redirects the browser there, ending the SSO session (not just the local
142	  app session).
143	- **`rsc-report-viewer/src/main/resources/templates/tps-utilization.html:168`,
144	  `daily-status-analysis.html:163`, `daily-transaction-summary.html:168`** — Report file download
145	  links across all three report screens now point at `/download/{type}/{fileName}`, matching
146	  `ReportingController`'s actual `@GetMapping("/download/{type}/{fileName}")` mapping (no
147	  `/reporting` prefix); this was previously broken only for the TPS report link.
148	
149	## Summary
150	Blocker: 2. Should-Fix: 4. Note: 3. Business rules/behaviors discovered: 9.
151	This is advisory input for test-planner's risk rating and human review — it does not gate or
152	block the pipeline.
